Chapter 20
 1. What is epilepsy? What are the signs and symptoms of 
epilepsy?
Epilepsy is a neurological disorder characterized by 
recurrent seizures, generally more than two unprovoked
seizures. A seizure can occur in either a portion of or the 
entire brain and typically presents as sudden deviations in 
the way the person feels or acts. For example, the patient
may experience a change in smell, vision, or hearing. Pos-
sible signs include staring, muscle jerking, twitching, head 
drops, falls, incontinence, salivation, cyanosis, and/or loss 
of consciousness.
